learningObjective: Diagnose the performance impact of register spilling on GPU kernels and identify why 'local memory' spills traverse HBM.

requiredFeatures: per-thread local memory backed by global memory

profileData: ptxas info: Used 255 registers, 0 bytes cmem[0], 128 bytes stack frame, 128 bytes spill stores, 128 bytes spill loads.
stem: You compile a CUDA kernel and ptxas reports `128 bytes spill stores, 128 bytes spill loads`. Which statement about GPU register spills is correct?

options.text: Spill loads/stores traverse per-thread 'local memory', which physically resides in HBM (cached in L1/L2). Each spilled access can add hundreds of cycles of latency and adds HBM bandwidth pressure, especially if L1/L2 do not absorb the traffic.
Spills go to a dedicated on-chip spill buffer separate from HBM and L1/L2, so spill traffic does not consume DRAM bandwidth.
Spills go to shared memory automatically; the ptxas 'spill' counters report shared-memory bytes rather than HBM bytes.
Spills are always harmless because L1 hits them; the compiler only spills if it has proven the access will hit cache on the next reload.

explanation: CUDA per-thread 'local memory' is a logical name; physically it lives in HBM (global memory) with L1/L2 caching. Spill stores/loads therefore incur potentially hundreds of cycles of latency and consume HBM bandwidth when L1/L2 do not absorb the traffic. Options B, C, D contradict the CUDA memory model.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: local memory backs spills; physically resides in HBM with L1/L2 caching.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: there is no separate on-chip spill buffer; spills go to logical local memory backed by HBM.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: shared memory is programmer-managed and finite per block; the compiler does not implicitly spill registers to shared memory.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the compiler does not have general proof of cache residency; spills are decided by register-pressure heuristics, and their runtime cost varies.

assumptions: ptxas reports spill counters when register pressure exceeds a threshold controlled by --maxrregcount or -Xptxas -O.
Local memory is caching per NVIDIA's memory model (L1/L2 involvement).
nonImplications: Does not imply that every spill costs a full HBM latency; L1/L2 can hit repeatedly-used spill slots.
Does not imply reducing register count via --maxrregcount always improves performance; forcing spills may be worse than accepting lower occupancy.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses shared memory with logical local memory.
distractorRationales.D: Overstates compiler's knowledge of cache behavior.

sourceRefs.locator: Local memory section; register file and spills

performanceClaim.scope: ptxas spill diagnosis on NVIDIA GPUs
